results.title: Prioritizing global equity in migration research - Nature
results.content: Migration research has largely centered on subjects, locations, and priorities of interest to higher-income countries (Amelung et al., 2024 Reinventing the politics of knowledge production in migration studies: Introduction to the special issue. Figure 4 shows the distribution of country salience in migration research, alongside the geographical composition of authors’ affiliations by country income groups. Overall, the two sets of models show that research salience in the migration field is strongly associated with countries’ geographic location and economic resources, particularly for those with a high income and higher level of research investment. Scholars have suggested and presented anecdotal evidence of a disparity in terms of country research on migration (Amelung et al., 2024 Reinventing the politics of knowledge production in migration studies: Introduction to the special issue. While we set out to measure, identify, and explain the concentration of migration research salience in terms of underrepresented countries, there are various other gaps to be identified systematically, such as populations, topics, epistemologies, and methods, among others (Castro Torres and Akbaritabar, 2024 The use of linear models in quantitative research.

results.title: Migration and Development Initiative
results.content: # Migration and Development Initiative. The Migration and Development Initiative was launched in 2019 to use cutting-edge social science methods to study migration and development where it matters most – including West and Central Africa, the Middle East, and Central America’s Northern Triangle. Starting from the principle that migration can lead to better development outcomes around the world, the initiative tests interventions designed to improve the process for everyone involved: the people who migrate, the countries who receive them, and the communities they leave behind and sometimes rejoin. The initiative developed a WhatsApp survey method and has used it to study Syrians in Lebanon and Venezuelans in Colombia; created a database of every nation’s asylum and refugee policies dating back to 1951 in partnership with the World Bank and United Nations; and is leading a randomized control trial, called Planning for Productive Migration (PPM), in Niger to study if training and cash assistance programs can help underemployed rural men improve their outcomes during seasonal migration to urban centers.
